rule: Expected observations are literal review of each plan under vm/SPEC.md, written before any VM run (D7); golden rows reuse vm/golden images with invocations the goldens do not freeze. The ceiling section states its own provenance: its bump pointers were first measured, and are now derived from section 5. The nat-pred limited rows state theirs: a draft slip, caught by a pre-fix VM run before commit, was corrected by rederiving from sections 5 and 6. The growth rows state theirs: their stops are derived from sections 5 and 7 by check-core's `loop_stop`, and their memory.grow bound is the growth policy's (CORE.md choice 15), fixed before the VM changed. limited.name: nat-pred-frames
limited.basis: Section 5: the image ends at byte 4,664, so F0 = 65,536 and H0 = F0 + 16 MiB = 16,842,752. A cell is 2 header words plus its payload, rounded to a power of two of at least 4 words (check-core's `cell`). Boot pushes Top(0) (3 words, section 6), so top = F0 + 12, and materializes the pool's Big 2^31 + 1 (payload 1: 16 B). main's entry is a tail entry below Top (section 6.2): no Call frame; its Activation (owner, depth and 2 slots: payload 4, 6 words, so 8) is 32 B, so bump = H0 + 48. Eval Let pushes Bind (top F0 + 24); its Return pops it and pushes Scope (F0 + 24). Eval Case selects Succ (section 6.1: selection allocates nothing), pushes Scope(depth), and only then allocates the predecessor 2^31, a Big of 16 B (vm-spec D17: the allocation follows the push). Completed, the run ends at H0 + 64, which check-core's section 5 model (`ceiling_run`) also gives for this plan. With a 24-byte frame region the Case's Scope needs F0 + 36: Exhausted kind 3 (frames) before anything is written, so the predecessor is never made: top = F0 + 24 = 65,560 and bump = H0 + 48 = 16,842,800. A VM that made the predecessor before the push would stop with bump H0 + 64. Provenance: a first draft of this row left out the cells' 2 header words (an Activation of 16 B, and a 32-byte heap); a run of the pre-fix VM, before the row was committed, exposed the slip. Every value here was then rederived from section 5's cell rule (check-core's `cell`) and section 6's 3-word frames; in the gate, `ceiling_run` under the lowered heap checks the heap row's bump, and both `top` values and the frames row's bump rest on this hand derivation. The pins that tell the two orders apart differ from the pre-fix VM's (80bd5cf)

ceiling.rule: Images whose bump pointer ends within 16 MiB of 4 GiB, where describe used to reserve a 16 MiB text window and a worklist above it in 32-bit arithmetic (review round 2), and, from review round 4, images whose last cell ends exactly at 4 GiB, which section 5 allows (only a cell ending beyond the maximum stops). Provenance: c9869ef chose the first six plans' fill counts a and b by measuring the pre-fix VM's bump pointer, and pinned `bump` from that measurement; review round 3 found it labelled literal review. The gate now derives every row before any VM runs: check-core's `ceiling_run` sums SPEC section 5's cell sizes over the plan (no reclamation, CORE.md choice 1; append as one block, choice 4), stops at a cell that would end beyond 4 GiB with Exhausted kind 2 (heap), and `ceiling_expectation` completes a Program at its Emit and starts a Book's text at the bump pointer (choice 12). Each `expect` and `dump` must equal that derivation; it agrees with every measured pin, so no value changed. The four rows at exactly 4 GiB chose their fill counts from that model alone, before any VM ran them. Each basis records the arithmetic. Each run touches about 4 GiB, so at most two run at a time, each in its own process.

growth.rule: Small cells reach the heap's end, or a host's refusal to grow, in bounded time. SPEC section 5 leaves the timing of memory.grow free and section 11 counts a timeout as neither Exhausted nor agreement, so a VM that grows memory one 64 KiB page at a time fails here: V8 pays each grow in the size of the memory, 22 minutes at 4 GiB (review round 1), by its wall time (loop-4gib) and by its memory.grow count (loop-256mib). One image, core/loop-cells (review round 1's probe, byte for byte), whose every entry allocates one 16-byte Activation, so no other cell or block hides the growth. Each row's stop is derived by check-core's `loop_stop` from sections 5 and 7 in closed form, which agrees with the entry-by-entry `ceiling_run` at a 1 MiB heap; the expectations were frozen before the VM's growth policy changed (CORE.md choice 15).

rows.name: loop-256mib
rows.basis: Sections 5 and 7: the image ends at byte 4,456, so F0 = 65,536 and H0 = F0 + 16 MiB = 16,842,752; the pool is empty. main's entry and each of loop's is debited (calls += 1, section 7 step 1) and then takes an Activation of 0 slots: payload 2 words, a cell of 4 words, 16 bytes. A heap lowered to 256 MiB ends at H0 + 268,435,456 = 285,278,208 and holds exactly 16,777,216 cells; the next entry is debited (call 16,777,217) and its Activation would end beyond the heap: Exhausted kind 2 (heap), bump unchanged at 285,278,208. memory.grow calls: the VM grows memory in steps of 16 MiB (CORE.md choice 15), and 285,278,208 bytes lie within the first 288 MiB, so at most 18 grows (one per 16 MiB, boot included); 24 leaves room. Growing one 64 KiB page at a time takes about 3,800.

rows.name: loop-4gib
rows.basis: As loop-256mib with the heap at its 4 GiB maximum (D19): (2^32 - 16,842,752) / 16 = 267,382,784 cells fill it exactly, the last ending at 2^32, which section 5 allows (only a cell ending beyond the maximum stops). The next entry is debited as call 267,382,785 and its Activation would end beyond it: Exhausted kind 2 (heap) with bump 2^32, and the real host shows `Exhausted io memory`. Review round 1 measured the VM that grew one page at a time at 22 min 45 s wall on this row, against a 120 s guard here.

rows.name: loop-refused
rows.basis: A host that refuses memory.grow beyond 4,700 pages (node --wasm-max-mem-pages=4700), 308,019,200 bytes, below the 4 GiB maximum. Section 5: that is HostFailure, never Exhausted; the real host shows `HostFailure io trap`, exit 5, and the VM has no outcome of its own (its register stays 0). The cells tile H0..308,019,200 exactly ((308,019,200 - 16,842,752) / 16 = 18,198,528), so bump = 308,019,200 and the next entry, debited as call 18,198,529, is the one refused. The cap is 293.75 MiB, not a multiple of 16 MiB: a VM that traps when its 16 MiB step is refused would stop 5.75 MiB lower, at 301,989,888. It must fall back to the size it needs (CORE.md choice 15).

memory-end.rule: A cell that ends exactly at the end of the memory in use. Boot grows memory once, to 48 MiB (the arguments sit at 0x2010000, CORE.md), and the heap grows it only when a cell would end beyond it, to the next 16 MiB boundary at or above the cell's end (CORE.md choice 15), so memory ends exactly where a cell does whenever that cell ends at such a boundary. A VM that reads or writes a word past a cell's end faults only there: anywhere else the access lands in the cell's padding or in free heap above the bump pointer, which `$alloc` zeroes before any cell holds it. Each row fills the heap from H0 with fill(k, B0{}), one 32-byte Activation and one 32-byte B1 cell per step, so that its last cell ends at 48 MiB. Section 5's model (check-core's `ceiling_run`) gives the fill count k, the pool constants that align the last cell, the bump pointer and the line; the reference evaluation of the same plan with k = 3 gives the line again and the calls, each further step being one entry of fill. The gate derives all of it again. `grows` is literal review of choice 15: boot's one grow, and one more for describe's text, which starts at the bump pointer, the memory's end. A probe of the VM (.local/vm-core/probe/r9/, review round 6's closing session) showed that three of the study's survivors trap on these Books and on no other row, before they were frozen.

rows.name: memory-end-object
rows.basis: main = let a = fill(523262n, B0{}) in let t = T4{1, 2, 3, 4} in case t of T4{a, b, c, d} -> On{}. The image ends at byte 5,288, so F0 = 65,536 and H0 = F0 + 16 MiB = 16,842,752, and the pool holds no cell (every literal is an immediate). main's Activation (6 slots: payload 8, 10 words, so 16) is 64 bytes; each of fill's k + 1 entries takes an Activation of 3 slots (payload 5, so 8 words: 32 bytes) and each of its k steps a B1 (payload 3: 32 bytes); T4 (4 fields: payload 6, 8 words) takes 32 more. So T4 ends at H0 + 128 + 64k = 50,331,648 = 48 MiB exactly, and fills its cell: the Case binds its four words, the last at 48 MiB - 4. describe writes `On{}` from 48 MiB, which grows memory once. 523,264 entries: main and fill k + 1 times

The pool holds "x" and "y" (a 32-byte SCon each) and the Big 2^31 (16 bytes): 80 bytes, which align the Action. main's Activation (4 slots) and IO.print's (1 slot) are 32 bytes each, fill's k + 1 Activations and k B1 cells 32 each, and the Action, a cell of its foreign id and its one operand (2 words, 4 with the header), 16. So the Action ends at H0 + 192 + 64k = 50,331,648 = 48 MiB exactly. describe writes `On{}` from 48 MiB, which grows memory once. 523,264 entries: main, fill k + 1 times and IO.print

reference.rule: Books whose expected run is literal review of the plan under SPEC sections 3 and 6, written before the VM change (D7), and which the gate also compares with vm-spec's reference evaluation (vm/evaluate.py `book`): the frozen run and `calls` must equal the reference's, and the VM's must equal both. Completing Chr{w} reads its operand as the reference's `construct` does (`word`), so a laundered non-scalar is ill-typed there, used or not (CORE.md choice 13; review round 3).

scope.rule: Images whose validation needs more scope indices than the tables' first size, W + 4200 for an image of W words (vm.wat `$validate`): a slot sits at the sum of the depths of the Closures around it, and a Branch binds every field of a constructor whose one record serves every Case that matches it (vm/scope.py). vm/scope.py builds each row's image from `family` and `args`; the gate requires its words, its `need` (the indices validation holds, derived from the plan alone) and its SHA-256 as frozen here. The verdicts and runs are the reference codec's and the reference evaluation's, fixed before the VM changed (D7): a valid image is admitted and its Book's `main` answers `On{}` (`Evaluated 1 1 On{}`, one call); a refused one is refused with the reference codec's first defect. `tables` and `edge` place an `edge-` row: its `need` is `edge` past the tables' size after `tables` doublings, (W + 4200) * 2^tables, so edge 0 fills them exactly and edge 1 makes the next doubling by one index (`unit`, `delta` do the same for a `nest-` row: the tables' first size is `delta` past the enclosing unit's depth, where the Closure's capture sits). `at_most` bounds the test build's memory.grow count at boot's one: the tables' successive sizes, at 5 bytes an index, sum to under 10 times their last, under 20 * need, and the loader's other tables take under 64 bytes a word of image, so the scratch of these rows is under 20 * need + 64 * W + 64 KiB, about 2 MB, and the 48 MiB that boot leaves holds it; tables that grow by one index at a time take gigabytes. Each `-past` row has a `-wrong` twin that declares the last slot at another type. Types are typed (K's fields cycle K, A, B, C) so that a slot read after a doubling shows whether its type was carried over. The first four rows are the reviewer's saved images, byte for byte (review round 1 of round 6), refused or trapped by the tables of W + 4200 indices that never grew. A `resource` row is valid by construction and needs more scratch than 4 GiB holds (`scope.scratch`): its frozen stop is the VM's, `Exhausted` kind 2 (heap), by the arithmetic of the tables' doubling, not the reference codec's, which is not run on it. Rows `excess-` are no scope rows: a unit deeper than its `slots` and a defect after that depth are reported as the defect, since the reference codec checks a unit's `slots` when the unit ends, so a validator that refused at the first depth beyond `slots` gives another reason.
